title: Build a frame for the console
description:
A text-mode game draws each frame by writing one string full of escape sequences. Write the pieces that build that string.

- `moveTo(row, col)` returns the sequence that moves the cursor to a position. **Your arguments count from 0**, as the rest of the game does; the sequence counts from 1. So `moveTo(0, 0)` is `"\x1b[1;1H"`.
- `colored(text, r, g, b)` returns `text` wrapped in a 24-bit colour sequence and a reset: `"\x1b[38;2;r;g;bm" + text + "\x1b[0m"`.
- `frame(map, playerRow, playerCol)` returns the whole frame: first the "cursor home" sequence `"\x1b[H"`, then every row of `map` followed by `'\n'`, with the character at the player's position replaced by `@`. If the player's position is outside the map, draw the map without them.

```
frame({ "#####", "#...#", "#####" }, 1, 2)
    == "\x1b[H#####\n#.@.#\n#####\n"
```
hints: `std::to_string(row + 1)` turns the 0-based row into the 1-based number the sequence wants.
In `frame`, copy each row before changing it, so the caller's map is left alone. Check the column is inside that row before writing the `@`.
